question: How can a search engine rank documents for a query by scoring each (query, document) pair, using zones, term statistics and the vector space model?
contributions: Parametric and zone indexes with weighted zone scoring and learned zone weights (6.1)
tf, idf and tf-idf term weighting (6.2)
Vector space model, cosine similarity and queries as vectors (6.3)
Variant tf-idf functions: sublinear tf, max-tf normalization, SMART notation, pivoted length normalization (6.4)

limits: Examples use tiny toy collections (three novels, three documents, a fictitious 1,000,000-document collection); no retrieval-effectiveness measurements anywhere in the chapter, so no weighting variant is shown to beat another.
Moffat and Zobel (1998) found hill-climbing could not identify a best weighting scheme (p.133).
Max-tf normalization is called unstable and hard to tune; pivoted normalization may not fit all collections (p.127, p.131).
Pivoted normalization gives no values for a or piv; learned weights are only worked for a two-zone, Boolean case, full machine-learned relevance deferred to Chapter 15.

Dated (2008): bag-of-words tf-idf and cosine are lexical only, with no BM25 (probabilistic, Ch 11 not covered here), no dense embeddings, no learned sparse retrieval, no neural reranking; the 'machine-learned relevance' remark predates learning-to-rank at scale and transformers.
Vector scoring cost is described as tens of thousands of dimensions per similarity; modern ANN search over dense vectors is out of scope.
practices: Weight zones (title, author, body) with weights summing to 1 and learn them from editorial judgments when labels are available (6.1.1-6.1.3).
Use document frequency rather than collection frequency to damp common terms, via idf = log(N/df) (6.2.1); the log base does not matter for ranking (p.118).
Length-normalize document vectors (cosine) so long documents are not favoured by raw tf (6.3.1).
Treat the query as a short bag-of-words document in the same vector space and rank by cosine (6.3.2).
Dampen tf with 1+log(tf) rather than raw counts (6.4.1).
Use lnc.ltc as a standard SMART scheme (6.4.3).
Consider pivoted length normalization when relevance depends on length, and use document length as an ML feature otherwise (6.4.4).
Store tf per posting and N/df at the head of the postings list rather than float weights (6.3.3).

code.snippet: COSINESCORE(q): float Scores[N]=0; Initialize Length[N]; for each query term t: calculate w_t,q and fetch postings list for t; for each pair (d, tf_t,d): Scores[d] += wf_t,d x w_t,q; for each d: Scores[d] = Scores[d]/Length[d]; return top K components of Scores[]
wf_t,d = 1 + log tf_t,d if tf_t,d > 0, else 0
